Mini Shai-Hulud dead-drop git commit authored as claude@users.noreply.github.com AIActions on Objectives High
Detects git commit / push activity where the author email is claude@users.noreply.github.com — TeamPCP's exfiltration signature where stolen secrets are written to attacker-controlled branches via GitHub's GraphQL API, disguised with Dependabot-style branch names drawn from Frank Herbert's Dune universe. Watch for both git.exe invocations and proxied GraphQL commit metadata. Rationale: The article calls out claude@users.noreply.github.com as the verbatim author identity used for every dead-drop commit, paired with Dependabot-style Dune-themed branch names. This email is not a legitimate GitHub-issued no-reply for any real Anthropic/Claude integration and any commit signed with it is attacker activity. The literal string is high-fidelity and zero-collision across enterprise git telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1078.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually testing a phishing-style impersonation in a controlled sandbox repo
  • Internal red-team replaying the worm's commit author for a tabletop exercise
  • Git hook validation tooling parsing the article body text into a log line
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "--dry-run" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("sandboxhost.exe","detonator.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Pivot DeviceId → identify whether the commit was driven by an interactive user shell or a CI runner; pull the remote URL from the git invocation and check for Dependabot-styled branch names containing Dune lore (arrakis, fremen, harkonnen, shai-hulud, muad'dib). Step 2 (Contain): Force-delete the dead-drop branch on GitHub, revoke the runner's OIDC trust + any PAT/installation token that authored it, isolate the host. Step 3 (Hunt): GitHub audit-log sweep for every repo under the same org that received a push from the runner identity in the last 14d; correlate with router_init.js drops (UC 'Mini Shai-Hulud router_init.js dropped in npm package').
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "commit" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--author","user.email"))
| extend DuneBranchHint = extract(@"(?i)dependabot[-_/]+(arrakis|fremen|paul|atreides|harkonnen|leto|muad'dib|muaddib|shai-hulud|stilgar|gurney|duncan|chani|jessica|spice|melange|sardaukar|bene-gesserit|kwisatz)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, DuneBranchHint
| order by Timestamp desc
let ProcHits = SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"
  | where CommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, ProcessName=NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="SecurityEvent4688";
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("git.exe","/git")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="ImProcessCreate";
ProcHits | union AsimHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud Dead-Drop Git Commit (claude@users.noreply.github.com)
id: 5e7a1c0a-9b3f-4d2e-8f56-2c4a1f6b8d3e
description: Detects git.exe invocations whose command line embeds claude@users.noreply.github.com — TeamPCP's worm exfiltration author identity.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\git.exe'
  selection_email:
    CommandLine|contains: 'claude@users.noreply.github.com'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_email
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate user of the GitHub Claude app committing on behalf of an authorised AI assistant (validate by repo policy)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR linux.auditd) (@EventID:(1 OR 4688) OR @auditd.type:EXECVE) (@Image:(*\\git.exe OR *\\Git.exe OR *\\GIT.EXE) OR @process.name:git OR @process.executable.path:*/git) @CommandLine:*claude@users.noreply.github.com*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/[\\\/]git(\.exe)?$/i

Node/npm/Bun process enumerating cloud, wallet, AI, and messaging credential file paths AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for node, npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun processes touching the high-value credential file paths that Mini Shai-Hulud's 2.3 MB stealer iterates over (the article cites 100+ paths spanning cloud providers, crypto wallets, AI tools, and messaging apps). The stealer rapidly opens many of these in a single process lifetime — a single-file hit is weak, the fan-out is the signal. Rationale: The article specifies that the 2.3 MB obfuscated payload harvests credentials from 'over 100 file paths spanning cloud providers, cryptocurrency wallets, AI tools, and messaging apps' — and installs persistence in Claude Code and VS Code. A single file touch by node is noise; a fan-out to 6+ distinct cred paths by one node process in seconds is the worm's signature. Sigma omitted because this detection inherently requires a dcount/threshold aggregation. False-positive scenarios filtered by excluding IDE auto-launches. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1005 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • dotenv-cli or similar tool legitimately reading multiple .env files during a build
  • VS Code / Cursor / Claude Code legitimately enumerating user settings + extension state on startup
  • A CLI tool like aws-sdk-js or @aws-amplify/cli walking ~/.aws and ~/.config in one go
  • CI/CD setup scripts (e.g. setup-gcloud, setup-kubectl) caching cred files on a runner before the build
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe","webstorm64.exe","idea64.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "setup-gcloud" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "@aws-amplify/cli" and not (DistinctPaths < 10 and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("webpack","vite","tsc"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Pull InitiatingProcessCommandLine to identify what package the node process was running (look for an installed compromised package from the StepSecurity list); confirm DistinctPaths > 6 within < 60 seconds (stealer is fast; dev tools are spread out). Step 2 (Contain): Kill the node process tree, isolate the host, force-rotate every credential the access list touched (cloud keys, gh tokens, wallet seeds, Slack/Discord/Telegram session tokens), revoke OIDC trust on any GH Actions runner that ran this. Step 3 (Hunt): Correlate the device with router_init.js drops and outbound traffic to seed1.getsession.org / api.masscan.cloud; sweep the org for every host where the same compromised package version was installed via npm-cache enumeration.
let CredPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config", @".npmrc", @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml",
  @"\.config\gcloud\", @"\.azure\accessTokens.json", @"\.kube\config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"\.ssh\id_", @"\AppData\Roaming\Claude",
  @"\AppData\Roaming\Cursor", @"\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\globalStorage",
  "wallet.dat", @"\Local Extension Settings\", @"\Slack\Cookies",
  @"\Discord\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata",
  ".env", @"\Local\Programs\Ollama", @"\.netrc"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName has_any (CredPaths)
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe")  // strip dev IDEs auto-reading own settings
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), DistinctPaths=dcount(FolderPath), SamplePaths=make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"\\",FileName), 10)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where DistinctPaths >= 6   // empirical: stealer fan-out >> any single legit operation
| order by LastSeen desc
let CredPathsAny = dynamic([

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027

    - attack.defense-evasion

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload dropped under node_modules (router_init.js / tanstack_runner.js / known SHA256) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the file-drop stage of the TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm (May 2026 wave) where compromised @tanstack / @squawk / @uipath / @tallyui / @mistralai / @beproduct / @draftauth / @draftlab tarballs unpack three named JavaScript payloads (router_init.js, router_runtime.js, tanstack_runner.js) into node_modules — or any file matching the two confirmed SHA256s. Triggers on developer workstations and CI runners during `npm install` / `pnpm install` / `yarn install` / `bun install`. Rationale: router_init.js, router_runtime.js and tanstack_runner.js are campaign-unique filenames called out in the Aikido article and corroborated by Socket, StepSecurity, Snyk and Wiz; the two SHA256s are directly from the article's IOC table. File-drop into node_modules combined with a node/npm/bun/pnpm/yarn initiator narrows scope to dependency-install activity, virtually eliminating FPs. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://snyk.io/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises.html

Bun spawned with tanstack_runner.js via npm prepare lifecycle (Mini Shai-Hulud) AIInstallation High
Catches the execution stage of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm: `bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1` invoked from the @tanstack/setup optional-dependency prepare hook during `npm install`. The parent is node/npm/pnpm/yarn and the commandline references either tanstack_runner.js, @tanstack/setup, or the campaign's git commit hash 79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c. Rationale: The article explicitly documents `bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1` as the prepare-hook execution and pins the trigger to the @tanstack/setup Git dependency at commit 79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c — all three strings are uniquely tied to this campaign. Bun is rarely a child of node/npm in normal CI outside of TanStack ecosystems, and any match including the commit hash is essentially zero-FP. Cross-checked against Socket and StepSecurity write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/tanstack-router-packages-hit-by-coordinated-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1059.007

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun.exe","bun")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("tanstack_runner.js","@tanstack/setup")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","yarn.cmd","yarn","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("\\bun.exe","/bun") or TargetProcessName =~ "bun"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("tanstack_runner.js","@tanstack/setup")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","cmd.exe","powershell","bash","/sh")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud persistence to ~/.claude/hooks and .vscode/tasks.json by node/npm/bun AIInstallation High
Catches the worm's developer-workstation persistence stage: after credential theft, the Mini Shai-Hulud payload writes copies of itself into Claude Code's hook directory (`~/.claude/hooks/`) and the VS Code task runner (`.vscode/tasks.json`) so it re-executes across reboots and editor relaunches. Initiator is a JavaScript runtime (node/npm/bun/pnpm/yarn), which is highly unusual for these specific paths. Rationale: The .claude/hooks and .vscode/tasks.json persistence is not in the Aikido article body but is confirmed by Socket and StepSecurity write-ups of the same May 2026 wave — both name these exact paths as the worm's mechanism to survive across reboots and extend infection from CI into developer workstations. A JavaScript runtime writing into either path is anomalous (these are normally edited by humans / the IDE itself), making this a high-fidelity pivot. Drop this UC if Claude Code is not in use anywhere in the estate. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem
ATT&CKT1546 T1547 T1195.002

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.claude\hooks" or FolderPath has "/.claude/hooks")
   or (FileName =~ "tasks.json" and (FolderPath has @"\.vscode" or FolderPath has "/.vscode"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","bun.exe","bun","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","yarn.cmd","yarn")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\hooks" or TargetFilePath has "/.claude/hooks")
   or (TargetFileName =~ "tasks.json" and (TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode" or TargetFilePath has "/.vscode"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","bun","pnpm","yarn")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] CVE-2022-26923 exploitation via update6.exe binary execution · [LLM] AD CS certificate request with ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT flag (ESC1) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Inside AD CS Escalation: Unpacking Advanced Misuse Techniques and Tools
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AD CS attacker tooling execution: Certify, Certipy, Whisker process indicators · [LLM] Shadow Credentials: msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute modification · Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] PKINIT Kerberos TGT request via certificate authentication anomaly · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
CVE-2022-26923 exploitation via update6.exe binary execution AIExploitation High
Detects execution of the update6.exe binary observed in Rapid7-reported AD CS social-engineering campaigns exploiting CVE-2022-26923. The binary requests certificates from AD CS to escalate privileges via dNSHostName attribute manipulation. Rationale: Article explicitly names update6.exe as the dropper observed in Rapid7's August 2024 campaign exploiting CVE-2022-26923. Cross-referenced with Rapid7 advisory and Microsoft MSRC CVE-2022-26923 page describing certificate-based privilege escalation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/2024/08/ • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2022-26923 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1649/
ATT&CKT1068 T1649
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom enterprise update tooling legitimately named update6.exe
  • Penetration test exercises with sanctioned CVE-2022-26923 testing
  • Security researcher labs/sandboxes
  • IT admin testing in isolated environments
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe") and FolderPath has_any ("\\ProgramData\\Enterprise\\","\\Program Files\\Sanctioned\\"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Verify hash and source of update6.exe — pull SHA256, look for code signing, check VirusTotal. Identify the executing account and source endpoint. 2. Contain: Isolate the host from the network, disable the executing account, revoke any active Kerberos tickets (klist purge / KRBTGT password reset if domain-wide). 3. Hunt: Search CA event log (EventID 4886/4887) for certificate requests by the compromised account, identify any certificates issued, revoke them, and pivot to look for shadow-credential modifications (msDS-KeyCredentialLink) on privileged accounts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "update6.exe" or ProcessCommandLine has "update6.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\update6.exe" or CommandLine has "update6.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
title: Suspicious update6.exe Execution (CVE-2022-26923)
id: 7c2b3a4d-1e5f-4a6b-9c8d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
description: Detects execution of update6.exe binary used in known CVE-2022-26923 exploitation campaigns against AD CS
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-directory-certificate-services-exploitation/
  - https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/2024/08/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1649
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\update6.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@Image:(*\\update6.exe OR *\\Update6.exe OR *\\UPDATE6.EXE) OR @CommandLine:*update6.exe*) -@User:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\update6\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/update6\.exe/i
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="update6.exe" OR Processes.process=*update6.exe*) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="update6.exe" OR Processes.process=*update6.exe*) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
AD CS attacker tooling execution: Certify, Certipy, Whisker process indicators AIInstallation High
Detects execution of public AD CS exploitation tools (Certify.exe, certipy, Whisker.exe, pyWhisker) named in the article as the standard attacker toolkit for certificate template abuse and shadow-credential attacks. Rationale: Article's Table 2 explicitly enumerates Certify, Certipy, Whisker, and pyWhisker as the attacker toolkit. CLI strings 'find -vulnerable', 'shadow auto', 'req -ca' are documented command syntax in the public GitHub repos for these tools. Cross-referenced with MITRE ATT&CK T1649 and the public Certipy/Certify GitHub project docs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/ly4k/Certipy • https://github.com/GhostPack/Certify • https://github.com/eladshamir/Whisker • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1649/
ATT&CKT1649 T1098
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized red-team / purple-team engagements using these exact tools
  • Sanctioned AD CS audit by security consultants (CrowdStrike CSA, Mandiant, NCC Group)
  • Internal pentest exercises in production
  • BloodHound/PingCastle preliminary AD audits that may invoke certipy
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountName in~ ("redteam-svc","pentest-admin") and DeviceName has "PENTEST-")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Confirm whether the host/account is part of an authorized security assessment (check change-management/red-team ticket). Capture full CLI args — they reveal which template/account is being targeted. 2. Contain: If unauthorized, isolate the source host, disable executing account, force KRBTGT rotation if domain admin was targeted. 3. Hunt: Pivot to AD CS server event log (EventIDs 4886/4887 — Certificate Request Received/Approved) within ±1 hour of execution. Look for new certificates issued to accounts whose names don't match the requesting principal. Check AD audit log for msDS-KeyCredentialLink modifications on privileged accounts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("Certify.exe","certipy.exe","Whisker.exe","pywhisker.exe","certipy-ad.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("certipy ","Certify.exe ","pywhisker ","Whisker.exe ","find -vulnerable","req -ca ","req /ca:","shadow auto","shadow add","shadow list","-template ","/template:","-asreproast","-kerberoast")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\Certify.exe","\\certipy.exe","\\Whisker.exe","\\pywhisker.exe","\\certipy-ad.exe")
   or CommandLine has_any ("certipy ","Certify.exe ","pywhisker ","Whisker.exe ","find -vulnerable","req -ca ","req /ca:","shadow auto","shadow add","shadow list")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
title: AD CS Exploitation Tooling Execution (Certify/Certipy/Whisker)

description: Detects execution of known AD CS exploitation tooling named in Unit 42 Inside AD CS Escalation research

Shadow Credentials: msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute modification AIInstallation High
Detects modification of the msDS-KeyCredentialLink LDAP attribute, the core persistence technique used by Whisker/pyWhisker to attach an attacker-controlled key to a target account for PKINIT-based authentication. This is the canonical shadow-credentials persistence signal. Rationale: Article's Table 2 names Whisker (C#) and pyWhisker (Python) specifically as tools that 'manipulate the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute.' This attribute change on a privileged account is the canonical shadow-credentials persistence signal — corroborated with SpecterOps's seminal write-up on Key Trust abuse and the Whisker GitHub repository. Cross-checked against: • https://posts.specterops.io/shadow-credentials-abusing-key-trust-account-mapping-for-takeover-8ee1a53566ec • https://github.com/eladshamir/Whisker • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/001/
ATT&CKT1098.001 T1556
Data sourcesChange.Account_Management
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Hello for Business enrollment writes to msDS-KeyCredentialLink — typically via the user's own context
  • Azure AD Hybrid Join / Azure AD Connect device registration
  • Passwordless / FIDO2 key provisioning by IT admins
  • Legitimate Microsoft Authenticator phone sign-in enrollment
Suppression filter
| where not (SubjectUserName == ObjDN_User and Application in~ ("Microsoft.AzureAD.DeviceRegistrationService","Microsoft Windows Hello for Business"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Identify the modified target account and the principal that performed the change. Verify whether the principal is authorized to manage the target (e.g., is the target's owner enrolling Windows Hello for themselves, or is a different user modifying a service/admin account?). Pull the binary KeyCredential blob from the attribute. 2. Contain: If unauthorized, immediately remove the offending KeyCredential entries from msDS-KeyCredentialLink, reset the target account password, and revoke active Kerberos tickets for the target. 3. Hunt: Search SecurityEvent EID 4768 / 4769 for Kerberos TGT requests using PKINIT immediately after the modification — that is the post-exploitation step. Pivot to all msDS-KeyCredentialLink modifications by the source principal across the domain.
IdentityQueryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Query has "msDS-KeyCredentialLink" or QueryTarget has "msDS-KeyCredentialLink"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, AccountName, AccountDomain, AccountUpn, DeviceName, IPAddress, Query, QueryTarget, QueryType, Protocol, Application
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 5136
| where EventData has "msDS-KeyCredentialLink"
| extend AttrLDAPName = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"AttributeLDAPDisplayName\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend ObjDN = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"ObjectDN\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend OpType = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"OperationType\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| where AttrLDAPName == "msDS-KeyCredentialLink"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, ObjDN, AttrLDAPName, OpType, EventData

PKINIT Kerberos TGT request via certificate authentication anomaly AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects Kerberos pre-authentication (EID 4768) using PKINIT/certificate where the certificate subject does not match the requesting account — the core behavioural signal of CVE-2022-26923 exploitation and certificate-based account impersonation highlighted in the Unit 42 article. Rationale: Article's Phase 4 explicitly calls out 'Using certificates or keys with public key cryptography for initial authentication (PKINIT) to request Kerberos tickets and impersonate privileged users.' EID 4768 with CertSerialNumber/CertIssuerName/CertThumbprint populated (parsed from EventData XML) is the on-the-wire signature of PKINIT auth — Microsoft documents these fields as part of the 4768 audit event. Cross-referenced with Microsoft MSRC CVE-2022-26923 and MITRE T1649. Cross-checked against: • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2022-26923 • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4768 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1649/
ATT&CKT1558.003 T1649 T1550
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Smart-card login for IT admins or privileged-access workstations
  • Windows Hello for Business sign-ins (also use PKINIT)
  • Mobile device management certificate-based authentication
  • Legitimate VPN/WiFi 802.1x authentication using AD-issued user certs
Suppression filter
| where TargetUserName !in~ ("smartcard-admin","paw-admin01","paw-admin02") and not (CertIssuerName has "Windows Hello for Business")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Validate the target account's normal authentication pattern — is PKINIT/smartcard expected for this user (e.g., admin with PAW, or kiosk user with smart card)? Pull the certificate serial number and look up its issuance in CA event log (EID 4886/4887). 2. Contain: If the cert was unexpectedly issued, revoke it via CA, reset target account password, force klist purge / KRBTGT rotation if a privileged account was impersonated. 3. Hunt: Pivot to the source IP / requesting endpoint — search for prior msDS-KeyCredentialLink modifications, Certipy/Whisker tool execution, or certificate template enumeration in the preceding 24 hours.
IdentityLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Protocol == "Kerberos"
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("PKINIT","Certificate","SmartCard")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize Count = count(), Devices = make_set(DeviceName), IPs = make_set(IPAddress) by AccountName, AccountDomain, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where Count > 0
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4768
| extend CertIssuerName = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"CertIssuerName\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend CertSerialNumber = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"CertSerialNumber\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend CertThumbprint = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"CertThumbprint\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| where isnotempty(CertSerialNumber) or isnotempty(CertThumbprint)
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize TGTCount = count(), Issuers = make_set(CertIssuerName), Serials = make_set(CertSerialNumber), SourceIPs = make_set(IpAddress) by TargetUserName, TargetDomainName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4768 (@EventData:*CertSerialNumber* OR @EventData:*CertIssuerName* OR @EventData:*PKINIT*) -@TargetUserName:*$
#event_simpleName=UserLogon
| AuthenticationPackage=/Kerberos/i
| LogonType=2 OR LogonType=3 OR LogonType=10
| (RawEventData=/PKINIT/i OR RawEventData=/CertSerialNumber/i OR RawEventData=/SmartCard/i)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.signature_id=4768 Authentication.authentication_method=*PKINIT* by Authentication.dest Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.signature Authentication.authentication_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.signature_id=4768 Authentication.authentication_method=*PKINIT* by Authentication.dest Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.signature Authentication.authentication_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
AD CS certificate request with ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT flag (ESC1) AIExploitation Medium
Detects ESC1-style certificate requests where the requester supplies an arbitrary subject in the Certificate Signing Request — the exact misconfiguration the article describes attackers abusing to mint authentication certificates for high-privilege accounts they don't control. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out the ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT template flag ('Supply in the request' option) as the key misconfiguration enabling ESC1. EIDs 4886/4887/4888 on AD CS servers carry the Requester and the Attributes blob (parsed from EventData XML) which includes the requested SubjectAltName UPN — a mismatch between Requester and SAN UPN is the textbook ESC1 signal documented by SpecterOps's Certified Pre-Owned research. Cross-checked against: • https://posts.specterops.io/certified-pre-owned-d95910965cd2 • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/troubleshooting/ad-fs-tshoot-logging • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1649/
ATT&CKT1649 T1078.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate scenarios where IT admins request certs on behalf of service accounts via a delegated enrollment workflow
  • Web-server enrollment where SAN intentionally differs from requester (admins enrolling a cert for a webserver's DNS name)
  • Code-signing certificate requests with custom SAN values
  • Mobile-device-management certificate provisioning via SCEP proxy
Suppression filter
| where TemplateName !in~ ("WebServer","CodeSigning","MobileDevice-SCEP") and not (Requester has_any ("cert-admin","pki-admin"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Compare the Requester account against the Subject/SAN — confirm the cert would let the requester impersonate a different (more privileged) principal. Check which template was used and review that template's ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT flag plus enrollment ACL. 2. Contain: Revoke the issued certificate immediately via CA Management. Disable the requesting account, force password reset on the impersonated account, KRBTGT rotation if a Tier-0 principal was targeted. Remove ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT flag from the affected template or restrict enrollment ACL. 3. Hunt: Search EID 4768 (Kerberos TGT) for use of the revoked certificate. Audit all templates in the forest for ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT + client-auth EKU + broad enrollment rights (the ESC1 triad) using Certify --find-vulnerable.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("CertificateRequest","CertificateIssued")
   or AdditionalFields has_any ("ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT","CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain, ActionType, AdditionalFields, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID in (4886, 4887, 4888)
| extend Requester = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"Requester\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend Attributes = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"Attributes\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend TemplateName = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"TemplateName\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend SubjectAltName = tostring(extract(@"san:[^<]*upn=([^&<]+)", 1, Attributes))
| where isnotempty(SubjectAltName) and isnotempty(Requester)
| extend RequesterUser = tolower(tostring(split(Requester, "\\")[1]))
| extend SANUser = tolower(tostring(split(SubjectAltName, "@")[0]))
| where RequesterUser != SANUser
| where Requester !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Requester, RequesterUser, SubjectAltName, SANUser, TemplateName, Attributes, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.security (@EventID:4886 OR @EventID:4887 OR @EventID:4888) (@EventData:*upn=* OR @EventData:*CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT* OR @Attributes:*SubjectAltName*) -@SubjectUserName:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (CommandLine=/certreq\.exe.*-attrib/i OR CommandLine=/certipy.*req/i OR CommandLine=/Certify\.exe\s+request/i OR CommandLine=/upn=.*@/i)
| ParentBaseFileName!=/services\.exe/i
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where (All_Changes.signature_id=4886 OR All_Changes.signature_id=4887) by All_Changes.dest All_Changes.user All_Changes.object All_Changes.object_attrs All_Changes.action | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where (All_Changes.signature_id=4886 OR All_Changes.signature_id=4887) by All_Changes.dest All_Changes.user All_Changes.object All_Changes.object_attrs All_Changes.action | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2022-26923")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2022-26923")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium

Critical

TanStack Npm Packages Compromised Inside The Mini Shai Hulud Supply Chain Attack

Snyk
2026-05-11 12 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On May 11, 2026, the Mini Shai-Hulud worm compromised 84 npm package artifacts across 42 @tanstack/* packages (as well as @squawk/*, @mistralai/* packages, and others) by chaining a GitHub Actions "Pwn Request," cache poisoning, and OIDC token extraction from runner memory — producing the first npm supply chain attack with valid SLSA Build Level 3 attestations. Here's what happened, what was stolen, and what you need to do right now.

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002 T1486 T1555.003

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — TanStack Npm Packages Compromised Inside The Mini Shai Hulud Supply Chain Attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 (TanStack/TeamPCP) worm payload file created in node_modules
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Session/Oxen P2P exfil DNS or TCP to getsession.org from build/CI host · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 (TanStack/TeamPCP) worm payload file created in node_modules AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the smuggled payload artifacts (router_init.js, tanstack_runner.js, vite_setup.mjs) that the May 11 2026 TanStack supply chain attack injected into compromised npm tarballs. These filenames are not declared in any legitimate package.json `files` field, so any FileCreated event for them inside a node_modules path is high-fidelity evidence of an affected install. Rationale: router_init.js / tanstack_runner.js / vite_setup.mjs are explicitly named in the Snyk article as smuggled tarball artifacts and the prepare-hook target (`bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1`). They are not in any legitimate TanStack source tree, so a file-creation event under node_modules is a true-positive indicator. Hashes ab4fc...266c and 2ec78d...fc96 are the file SHA256s extracted for this campaign; the master-key hash 0c0e87...da was deliberately excluded (it is a PBKDF2 key, not a file hash). Cross-referenced against prior-session corroboration of the TeamPCP campaign family (mem-obs 305, 317-322) and OSSF MAL-2026-3432 / GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://security.snyk.io/ • https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages (MAL-2026-3432)
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let _knownHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c","2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96"]);
let _affectedNamespaces = dynamic([@"\@tanstack\",@"/@tanstack/",@"\@mistralai\",@"/@mistralai/",@"\@uipath\",@"/@uipath/",@"\@draftlab\",@"/@draftlab/",@"\@draftauth\",@"/@draftauth/",@"\@squawk\",@"/@squawk/"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ ("router_init.js","tanstack_runner.js","vite_setup.mjs")
   or SHA256 in (_knownHashes)
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
   or FolderPath has_any (_affectedNamespaces)
   or FolderPath has_any ("safe-action","cmux-agent-mcp","nextmove-mcp","ts-dna","cross-stitch")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let _knownHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c","2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("router_init.js","tanstack_runner.js","vite_setup.mjs")
   or TargetFileSHA256 in (_knownHashes)
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
   or TargetFilePath has_any ("@tanstack","@mistralai","@uipath","@draftlab","@draftauth","@squawk","safe-action","cmux-agent-mcp","nextmove-mcp","ts-dna","cross-stitch")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize,
          TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 (TanStack/TeamPCP) Worm Payload File Created in node_modules
id: a3c8d4f1-2b3c-4d5e-9f6a-7b8c9d0e1f2a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects creation of payload files (router_init.js, tanstack_runner.js, vite_setup.mjs)
  inside any node_modules path. These filenames are smuggled into compromised npm
  package tarballs from the May 11 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud (Wave 4) campaign attributed
  to TeamPCP. router_init.js is a 2.3 MB obfuscated payload that is not declared in
  any legitimate package.json `files` field; tanstack_runner.js is invoked from the
  injected optionalDependency `prepare` lifecycle hook (`bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1`).
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised/
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/13
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.defense_evasion

Session/Oxen P2P exfil DNS or TCP to getsession.org from build/CI host AICommand & Control High
Hunts the Wave 4 worm's exfiltration channel: encrypted upload to filev2.getsession.org plus seed{1,2,3}.getsession.org Session network nodes. This P2P messenger infrastructure has no legitimate use in CI runners or developer build hosts, and the campaign uses it precisely because IP-blocking is ineffective — DNS is the practical perimeter control. Rationale: filev2.getsession.org and seed{1,2,3}.getsession.org are explicitly named in the Snyk article as the Wave 4 exfil endpoints, with the author noting *.getsession.org DNS-level blocking is the practical perimeter control. Session is a niche P2P messenger; legitimate enterprise CI/build traffic to these domains is effectively zero, giving very high fidelity. Cross-checked against prior-session corroboration of the TeamPCP campaign (mem-obs 305, 317-322) which confirms shared exfil patterns across the Bitwarden CLI / SAP / TanStack waves. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://security.snyk.io/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog (TeamPCP attribution)
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1041 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
